forces.title: Increased importance of PE purchase price discipline for returns
forces.description: Macro tailwinds that allowed private equity buyout funds to overcome elevated entry prices during 2010-2017 have diminished. In the 2018-2023 vintages, there's a clear performance divergence where disciplined buyers (lowest-price quartile) achieved significantly higher MOIC (3.4x) compared to those paying top prices (2.7x). This highlights a structural shift where fundamental pricing discipline is now a key determinant of PE returns.
forces.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters

forces.title: Rising global PE buyout entry multiples increasing investment risk
forces.description: Global buyout entry multiples reached a record average of 11.8x EBITDA, and 18.1x EBITDA for larger transactions (>$500 million) in 2025. While sponsors justify these premiums for 'A-grade' businesses, paying such high multiples, often with less leverage, significantly shrinks the margin for error for PE funds. This trend, driven by deployment pressures and competition, poses a headwind to achieving strong returns.
forces.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters

forces.title: Intense competition for quality PE assets driving up prices
forces.description: Private equity sponsors are facing increased competition for 'A-grade' businesses, with many B-grade and C-grade companies not coming to market or being pulled. This, combined with high deployment pressures, contributes to record-high entry multiples (e.g., 18.1x EBITDA for large buyouts in 2025), making it harder for PE funds to find attractively priced deals and achieve superior returns. This is a significant headwind for IN070406.
forces.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters

forces.title: Private equity deployment pressures risk overpaying for assets
forces.description: General partners (GPs) in private equity funds face intense pressure to deploy committed capital. This pressure contributes to their willingness to pay higher multiples for acquisitions, potentially leading to inflated entry prices. Such overpayment reduces the margin for error and can negatively impact fund returns, especially in an environment where macro tailwinds have diminished, presenting a key risk for IN070406 (Private Equity & Venture Capital).
forces.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters

forces.title: Strong M&A growth in digital infrastructure expands investment opportunities
forces.description: The digital infrastructure universe is rapidly expanding, with M&A deals in this sector increasing by over 60% in 2025. This growth, driven by technologies and services supporting the AI revolution, presents significant opportunities for investors. The expanding category now includes diverse assets like data centers, fiber, and power-linked assets, requiring refined due diligence from Capital Markets participants (IN070406, IN070402) to identify value.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: AI revolution reshaping digital infrastructure investment landscape
forces.description: The rapid rise of AI-dedicated assets, technologies, and services is increasingly dominating the digital infrastructure investment universe, blurring traditional boundaries. This structural shift necessitates that investors and operators adapt their underwriting and strategic frameworks to understand where value will accrue. Capital Markets firms (IN070406) need to refine their data-driven portfolio management and due diligence to capitalize on these new opportunities.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: Digital infrastructure investing facing increased complexity and risk
forces.description: The digital infrastructure universe has diversified into a complex, heterogeneous mix of hard assets, services, and resources, now heavily influenced by AI. This expanded scope means broad exposure to digital assets can lead to riskier outcomes, as value creation hinges on a wider array of asset-level portfolio choices. Capital Markets investors (IN070406) must adopt a more sophisticated, fundamentals-grounded due diligence approach to navigate this evolving landscape.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: Climate crises threaten municipal and sovereign bond markets
forces.description: Climate-induced crises are increasingly impacting municipal bonds and sovereign credit markets, leading to credit rating downgrades and higher borrowing costs. Global insured losses from natural catastrophes have quadrupled since 2000, while the capacity of capital markets to syndicate these losses has decreased by nearly two-thirds relative to the losses. This poses a significant risk to the Fixed Income, Debt & IBC (IN070405) sector, requiring stronger financial systems to absorb and distribute losses.
forces.source_title: Redesigning Climate Resilience for a World of Financial Tipping Points

forces.title: Capital markets crucial for climate risk mitigation solutions
forces.description: Escalating tail risks from climate change, evidenced by credit rating downgrades post-disasters, cannot be mitigated by private insurance alone. This necessitates that governments, businesses, and capital markets collaborate to fill the gap. Innovative solutions like parametric instruments and government-backed reinsurance pools demonstrate the potential for Capital Markets (IN070405, IN070402) to provide liquidity and risk-sharing, offering an upside opportunity for firms to develop and deploy financial instruments for increased volatility.
forces.source_title: Redesigning Climate Resilience for a World of Financial Tipping Points

forces.title: Climate risks not priced into municipal and sovereign bonds
forces.description: Climate risks are increasingly leading to credit rating downgrades and higher borrowing costs for municipal and sovereign bond markets globally. When these risks are not adequately priced in, it creates financial tipping points, impacting infrastructure financing and increasing debt servicing costs. Capital Markets participants, particularly those in Fixed Income, Debt & IBC (IN070405) and Ratings, Research & Data Providers (IN070404), face the risk of mispriced assets and reduced investor confidence without integrated risk assessments.
forces.source_title: Redesigning Climate Resilience for a World of Financial Tipping Points

forces.title: Government and regulatory push for climate resilience in financial services
forces.description: Governments and policymakers are actively working to realign incentives for businesses and financial services to address climate resilience. This includes undertaking broader risk assessments and convening multi-stakeholder solutions. Such initiatives create opportunities for Capital Markets firms (IN070405, IN070402) to participate in new funding structures, develop innovative financial instruments, and strengthen the overall financial system's capacity to absorb climate-related losses.
forces.source_title: Redesigning Climate Resilience for a World of Financial Tipping Points

forces.title: Capital markets adjusting investment strategies for climate risks
forces.description: The increasing visibility of climate-induced financial tipping points requires all financial services firms, including those in Capital Markets (IN070401, IN070405, IN070406), to adjust their investment plans. This involves looking beyond physical resilience to review financial and societal resilience, contributing to public-private risk pools, and deploying more financial instruments suited for increased volatility. This represents a fundamental shift in investment strategy and risk management for the sector.
forces.source_title: Redesigning Climate Resilience for a World of Financial Tipping Points

viewpoints.title: Purchase price discipline crucial for private equity buyout fund returns post-2017
viewpoints.description: In the 2018-2023 private equity vintage cluster, where macro tailwinds diminished, purchase price discipline became critical. Lowest-price quartile buyers generated 3.4x multiple on invested capital (MOIC), while highest-price buyers delivered only 2.7x. This contrasts sharply with the 2010-2017 boom where cheap financing allowed high entry prices without significantly penalizing returns, indicating a structural shift where price discipline is now paramount for PE success.
viewpoints.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters
